Alright, team, it's Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026, and the news cycle isn't taking a breath. Your daily briefing, fresh off the digital presses:

### Money Talk

- **Jensen Huang open to Nvidia return, faces Congress.**
  Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week amidst a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy and multiple employee affairs, is now signaling he'd be "honored" to return if the board asked. Meanwhile, Congress wants answers on whether Nvidia's AI chips were compromised. Talk about a dramatic comeback bid. [S5][S6][S14][S17][S18][S52]
- **Anthropic IPO eyed to validate AI valuations.**
  With hundreds of billions sloshing into AI startups, all eyes are on Anthropic's potential IPO. It's the litmus test venture investors need to prove their paper gains are real, and to set the stage for other smaller AI players looking for an exit. No pressure. [S2]
- **FAA router pause hits airline recovery, Home Depot dips.**
  The FAA has paused installation of new routers after a tech-induced nationwide ground stop caused chaos for travelers. Meanwhile, Home Depot shares are down despite beating earnings, showing even best-in-class can't escape a tough housing market. Infrastructure and housing, always a vibe check for the economy. [S1][S3][S16]
- **Kalshi pulls Trump markets after CFTC warning.**
  Prediction market platform Kalshi has yanked some Trump-related "mention" contracts at the CFTC's request. Apparently, betting on who mentions whom carries a "heightened manipulation risk." Sounds about right for anything involving that particular brand. [S4]
- **UK eyes 'polluter pays' levies for climate action.**
  The UK is backing a statement for new taxes on polluting sectors, including potential "frequent flyer" and crypto levies, to fund climate action costs. Brace for impact on your jet-set lifestyle and digital gold portfolios. [S12]

### World Lore

- **Iran ramps up strikes on US targets in Bahrain.**
  Iran just hit a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain with drones, marking its third attack in recent days. This comes after a two-month lull, and coincides with a gas tanker getting torched in the Strait of Hormuz. The Gulf is heating up again, watch your oil prices. [S11][S21]
- **Trump's Asia tour includes Xi-Putin summit on Ukraine.**
  President Trump is in Asia, kicking off in Manila before a planned three-way nuclear summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. He's apparently set to discuss Ukraine, which, conveniently, contradicts the White House's earlier agenda. Classic. [S22][S23][S25]
- **Ukraine hits key Russian bridge in Crimea.**
  Ukrainian forces struck a vital Russian rail and road bridge to the occupied Crimean Peninsula with drones and missiles. This wasn't some spur-of-the-moment thing, but a carefully prepared attack over weeks. Escalation, meet critical infrastructure. [S24]
- **US chip restrictions aim to curb China's AI ambitions.**
  New US rules are tightening chip exports to Southeast Asia, specifically designed to hit China's access to both advanced chips and their computing power. This is less about supply chains and more about a full-on tech-war chokehold. [S10][S51]
- **Russia wants NATO rollback to 1997 borders.**
  In a move that feels straight out of a history textbook, Russia is reportedly demanding NATO withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe, essentially rolling back its expansion to 1997. Moscow's trying to rewrite geopolitical history, good luck with that. [S35]

### Tech Tea

- **OpenAI drops GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Microsoft counters with MAI Code 2.**
  Not to be outdone by Microsoft's new MAI Code 2, OpenAI just unveiled GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. The AI arms race is moving at warp speed, and if you're not keeping up, you're already behind. Which models will get traction with developers is the real battle. [S36][S39]
- **Apple services hit by major outage.**
  iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, you name it – Apple's key services are down today. The status page confirms it, but no word on the cause. Hope you didn't need to download anything important or, you know, use your phone. [S37][S38][S42]
- **Google's Gemini "Tasks" now free, keeps chats for two months.**
  Google's AI agent, formerly Spark, is now "Tasks" and it's free, powered by their new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. It can handle calls, make purchases, organize your calendar. Oh, and it'll keep your chats for two months now, even if history is off. Convenient, or slightly creepy? You decide. [S41][S43][S46]
- **FAA grounds its own tech upgrade after nationwide stop.**
  After a software glitch caused a nationwide ground stop on Friday, the FAA has hit the brakes on installing new routers. It's a humbling moment for anyone banking on seamless tech rollout. Maybe test it before it takes down an entire country's air travel? Just a thought. [S1][S16]
- **Meta tests standalone Instagram messaging app "Direct."**
  Meta's trying a new messaging app called "Direct" in Turkey and Thailand, essentially stripping Instagram's DMs out into their own app. Feels a bit like deja vu, but hey, if it means less scrolling through Reels to answer a message, I'm not complaining. [S47]

### Creator Szn

- **YouTube inflates view counts with "co-views."**
  YouTube's now counting estimated "co-views" — people watching together on TV — into public view counts. So, your favorite creator's numbers just got a boost, but is it organic? Feels like a participation trophy for engagement metrics. [S49]
- **Creator vs. Influencer: The industry can't agree.**
  Marketers are still grappling with what actually constitutes a "creator" versus an "influencer" or "tastemaker." It's a semantic debate that probably only matters to agencies and LinkedIn gurus, but it highlights the Wild West nature of digital branding. [S57]
- **Dentsu doubles down on entertainment and sport.**
  With media revenues slipping, Japanese holding company Dentsu is making entertainment and sport a C-suite priority, appointing Mike Nakamura as chief. A clear signal they're chasing where the eyeballs (and wallets) are migrating in a fragmented landscape. [S59]

### Supply Lines

- **Pedestal AI raises $4.7M to "agentify" supply chains.**
  Logistics startup Pedestal AI just bagged $4.7 million to deploy "agentic AI" in supply chains, aiming to make them faster and more reliable. Sounds like the industry is finally ready to let the machines handle the unexpected, or at least help predict it. [S45]
- **SmartKargo launches AI apps for cargo industry.**
  SmartKargo is rolling out its first four AI applications designed to sit on top of any cargo system. They promise quick deployment and targeted P&L improvements, showcasing a practical application of AI that moves beyond just hype. [S61]
- **Amazon expands fuel surcharge to more services.**
  Starting in February, Amazon is extending its 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge to bulk storage and replenishment services. Expect that to trickle down the chain as companies grapple with fuel costs and Amazon passes the buck. [S69][S90]
- **DHL Supply Chain's global revenue grows, new Texas hub opens.**
  DHL Supply Chain is reporting 12% year-on-year sustainable revenue growth, driven by demand for more resilient supply chains. They also just completed their largest warehouse at a new North Texas campus. Seems like their strategy of handling everyone else's logistical headaches is paying off. [S76][S78][S80]
- **Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd restore Suez routes.**
  After bypassing it for a while, Gemini Cooperation partners Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd are restoring their Asia-Europe services to the Suez Canal in a phased rollout through mid-January. This *should* ease some congestion, but with Red Sea overcapacity still looming, rates might stay elevated for a bit. [S62][S64][S71]

### Speed Round

- Jensen Huang wants his old job back, and Congress wants a chat.
- The FAA's new routers failed, so now they're just... not installing them.
- Trump's in Asia, and his itinerary seems to be a moving target.
- Apple's services are down, proving even the big guys aren't immune to "have you tried turning it off and on again?"
- Ukraine just took out a major Russian bridge, another win for drone warfare.
- Google's Gemini "Tasks" will organize your life, and remember all your chats doing it.
- Your favorite YouTube creator's view count just got a little fuzzy with "co-views."
